authentication: OIDC bearer identity and a device session

deviceSession.open: the device signs kodosi-device-session-v1, the length-prefixed account id, device id and challenge id, and the 32-byte challenge; the server answers with a session secret
deviceSession.use: headers X-Kodosi-Device-Id and X-Kodosi-Device-Session on each device request and the deviceSession field of the device connection hello
deviceSession.refusal: status 428 when the server does not hold the session; the device opens a new session and sends the request again
deviceSession.storage: in the memory of the one serving process; 12 hours; removed with the device
deviceSession.changes: one change at a time for each account; reads do not wait

accountDeletion.signInService: with Auth:AccountDeletion set, GET /api/me gives deletionUri: the Keycloak action delete_account through the issuer's account-console client with a fresh PKCE challenge that nobody redeems; the person confirms there and Keycloak deletes the sign-in account
accountDeletion.feed: every 15 seconds the server reads DELETE_ACCOUNT user events and DELETE USER admin events of the last day with a client that has only the realm-management role view-events, and deletes the Kodosi account of each subject; after a start it reads 30 days
accountDeletion.direct: without Auth:AccountDeletion, deletionUri is null and DELETE /api/me deletes the account after a sign-in of at most 15 minutes; with it, DELETE /api/me answers 409
accountDeletion.removed: the account, its devices, device lists, links and recovery data, its friend list and friendships, its terminals and their sharing, the rooms it owns with their content, its room memberships and invitations
accountDeletion.kept: the room items it wrote in rooms of other people stay without an account
accountDeletion.afterwards: for 30 days the server keeps the issuer and subject and answers 410 to a token whose auth_time, or iat, is not after the deletion; a later sign-in starts a new account

identityRead.tag: GET /api/me/identity and GET /api/users/{userId}/identity give an ETag made of the identity incarnation and the device list generation
identityRead.unchanged: status 304 without a body when If-None-Match is equal to the tag

operation.migration: the argument migrate applies the schema and exits; a serving start refuses a database that is not current
operation.refusedConnections: one log line for each refused device connection with account, device and reason
operation.meter: Kodosi.Server: kodosi.device.connections, kodosi.relay.pipes, kodosi.relay.bytes, kodosi.connections.refused by reason, kodosi.database.fault in seconds

sessionAuthorization.ownDevices: current approved devices of the owner
sessionAuthorization.friends: explicit membership in the selected live publication
sessionAuthorization.administration: owner; membership updates require the hosting device
sessionAuthorization.rooms: all current members of the room to which the terminal was shared, including later members

sessionPublication.membershipMutation: replace chosen friend IDs with expected authorizationRevision
sessionPublication.revocation: advance the revision; close the relay pipes of removed people and devices at once; tell the host
sessionPublication.missingRecovery: current hosting device may republish same still-live incarnation with owner-only access

deviceLink.code: 12 random symbols of Crockford base 32 (60 bits) that the new device makes and shows; the server never gets it
deviceLink.key: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512, 1048576 rounds, password = the code as shown, salt = kodosi-device-link-v2 and the 16-byte nonce of the request, 32 bytes
deviceLink.requestProof: HMAC-SHA256 with the key over the length-prefixed fields: request, account id, device id, label, signing key
deviceLink.approvalProof: HMAC-SHA256 with the key over the length-prefixed fields: approval, account id, device id, identity root
deviceLink.identityRoot: SHA-256 of kodosi-identity-root-v1 and the certificate body of the one self-signed device of the account
deviceLink.request: the new device sends its device id, label, signing key, nonce and request proof; at most 5 open requests for each account; 10 minutes, which the new device also counts itself
deviceLink.approve: the approving device signs only the request whose request proof holds for the code that the user typed, and sends the approval proof
deviceLink.accept: the new device takes the account identity only when the approval proof holds for the identity root of the identity that it reads
deviceLink.server: stores and lists the requests and the two proofs; makes and checks no code

recoveryKey.text: 32 random symbols of Crockford base 32 (160 bits) that an approved device makes and shows one time; the server never gets it
recoveryKey.keys: HKDF-SHA256 with salt = the length-prefixed fields kodosi-recovery-v1, account id, identity root; the labels signing, device and room-key give the ML-DSA-65 seed, the device id (UUID version 8) and an AES-256-GCM key
recoveryKey.entry: one more device in the signed device list, with a certificate from the approved device that made it; an account has one; it cannot open a device session and a host refuses it
recoveryKey.roomKey: the entry has a room recipient key; the request that adds the entry carries the public part, signed with the recovery key, and the secret part sealed with the AES-256-GCM key, and the server stores both in one write
recoveryKey.recover: a signed-in device that has the text proves possession of its own key and sends its certificate and the next device list, both signed with the recovery key; the device keeps the room key pair of the entry until it has its own room keys in each room, then deletes it

friendIdentity.record: for each friend the user keeps: handle, identity root (absent until the first read), verified
friendIdentity.list: JSON of the records with the account id, a revision and the signing device id; signed with ML-DSA-65 over kodosi-friend-list-v1 and the body by an approved device of the account
friendIdentity.storage: the server stores the newest signed list of each account and replaces it only from the revision that the device read; it cannot make or change a list
friendIdentity.use: a device reads the identity of another account only with a record, and only when the identity root is equal to the root of the record
friendIdentity.created: by the user: a friend request, an accepted request, Trust, or Verify with an invite text
friendIdentity.hint: the friend list from the server gives identityIncarnationId for each friend so that a device can show a changed identity early; the hint is not trusted

missionContent: directory metadata only; no chat, tasks, or agent dispatch
backendSecrets: none; the server relays TLS records between a host device and a viewer device and holds no terminal key

roomContent.encryption: AES-256-GCM content keys; each recipient key is ML-KEM-768 and X25519 together, with HKDF-SHA256 over both shared secrets for the wrapping key; ML-DSA-65 signed state and content
roomContent.history: new members receive current room keys and decrypt the backwards-wrapped key history
roomContent.membership: signed room state commits member identities; removal rotates the content key; a member whose identity is not available keeps the last identity in the state; only the owner gives a member a new identity, with new keys; the relay holds no plaintext key
roomContent.content: immutable messages and versioned task/repository records; read by room sequence; compare expected version on updates
